SHA-1 is used only to reconstruct and compare the existing Git blob/tree object format, with usedforsecurity=False. It is not used for passwords, credentials, signatures or package integrity. The installed payload inventory, wheels, provenance and final installer use SHA-256.

The two flagged calls execute the literal git binary with separate -C, operator-selected source path, ls-files and -z argv values. No shell is used, no application request can select the command, and the build verifies the selected source tree before staging its files.

Health probes use recorded loopback URLs or an installing operator-selected private configuration endpoint, validated as HTTP(S) without embedded credentials/query/fragment. No application request input or tenant API key reaches the URL; probes carry no credential headers, use a three-second timeout, and retain default TLS certificate verification.

The test constructs the known Git blob object identifier to compare the source manifest against git write-tree. SHA-1 is required by this existing Git object format and is not a package-integrity, password or credential mechanism. Production payload digests remain SHA-256.
